text: Jazzercise is a fitness franchise company founded by Judi Sheppard Missett in 1969 and headquartered in Carlsbad, California, United States. The franchise's name is a portmanteau of "jazz" and "exercise." Missett created Jazzercise in Evanston, Illinois in 1969 after graduating from Northwestern University with a degree in theater and dance, where she studied with renowned jazz choreographer Gus Giordano at his Evanston studios. While teaching at a dance studio, she observed high dropout rates and realized students attended for physical fitness rather than performance, so she began holding "just for fun" classes that started with a jazz warmup. These classes, originally named "Jazz Dance for Fun and Fitness," were later renamed "Jazzercise." After her family moved to Carlsbad, California, she taught classes in local rec centers, and Jazzercise quickly gained popularity in San Diego, with Missett training new instructors herself. Many of these early instructors were from military families, allowing the program to spread across the country and worldwide. Initially using VHS videos, Missett trained franchisees remotely and began selling franchise rights. She also produced recorded Jazzercise programs for home use, starting with an LP titled *Jazzercise* in 1981, which was certified gold in 1982, followed by a second LP, *More Jazzercise*, in 1982, and her first VHS workout, *Let's Jazzercise*, the following year. Jazzercise was introduced by Jerome Somers to Campbell Union SD in 1993 as part of the school's physical education curriculum. Jazzercise is claimed on *A Bit of Fry & Laurie* to be a portmanteau of "jazz" and "circumcise." In Ron Howard's live-action film *How the Grinch Stole Christmas*, the Grinch's schedule includes an hour for Jazzercise. In the *Taxi* episode "Louie Goes Too Far," Latka Gravas suggests Reverend Jim Ignatowski take up Jazzercise to meet beautiful women. On *The Golden Girls*, Dorothy Zbornak admits to taking Jazzercise in the episodes "The Stan Who Came to Dinner" and "The Audit." In *Troop Beverly Hills*, lead character Phyllis Nefler states she hasn't been to Jazzercise in three weeks after chasing a troop member who suddenly runs off. In the *Futurama* episode "Parasite Lost," parasitic worms are seen Jazzercising Fry's muscles. In *The Flight of the Conchords* season 2 episode "New Zealand Town," the song "Fashion is Danger" parodies 1980s music and style and references Jazzercise. "Jazzercise Instructor" is a job featured in *The Sims 2*. In the third series of *The Mighty Boosh*, Howard Moon attends Jazzercise classes. In the *Glee* episode "Bad Reputation," a tape is found of Sue Sylvester Jazzercising to Olivia Newton-John's "Physical"; in the following season's episode "Sexy," Holly Holliday is shown teaching a Jazzercise class in which Will Schuester participates. On *The Goldbergs*, Beverly Goldberg frequently references or steps to Jazzercise. In the October 9, 2012 episode of *The Daily Show*, Jon Stewart referenced Jazzercise in his opening monologue. Jazzercise was featured in both *People* magazine and *Harper's Bazaar* in 2018. It was also featured at the fictional Starcourt Mall in season 3 of *Stranger Things*, where Dustin Henderson and Steve Harrington chase a suspicious-looking man they believe is from the Soviet Union, who turns out to be a Jazzercise instructor. Jazzercise was mentioned in the song "Party with Your Body" (from the album *All in a Night's Work*) by KC and the Sunshine Band and in the *Rick and Morty* season 6 episode "Juricksic Mort," when dinosaurs list things humanity has accomplished.
